mine_p09_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_001.text: On Day 535 the public meeting occupied the covered inspection office beside the gallery entrance. Lin arrived before her paid afternoon shift and found Chen Rui already speaking with Sui Jun. His voice made the crowded room sound orderly. He stopped when she approached, named the company account that retained him for the proposed method comparison, and asked whether she wanted the public explanation first. She did. Familiarity was not agreement. Lin took a seat where she could leave without crossing the speaker's table and put her three questions on her knee.

mine_p09_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_002.text: Qiao explained that the company wanted a finite comparison of practical method limits after the current gallery inspection work. No laboratory post had been offered to Lin, no qualification had been earned beyond six pairs, and no wages from a future comparison belonged to her yet. The proposed work might be useful to the mine, but it would need qualified candidates, actual consent for private technique material, and a defined account. Sui wanted the explanation to sound less uncertain. Chen said uncertainty belonged in the offer while the task was still being designed.

mine_p09_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_003.text: Chen then described the company's interest in reusable findings. A practical failed attempt could be valuable if it identified conditions a later worker should avoid. He spoke of method material as if knowledge naturally wanted to travel toward the best equipped bench. Lin asked who would own her private sensory record. Chen paused and answered that this proposal did not transfer it. Her permission for a particular retained copy would need its own scope. The pause mattered. A persuasive general phrase had reached farther than the actual offer, and he corrected it in front of witnesses.

mine_p09_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_004.text: Luo Bin sat beside Ma Lian on the worker bench. He was appointed to help workers with particular claims, not to grant blanket consent for everyone employed at the mine. He wanted practical safety warnings public even if private techniques stayed confidential. Chen agreed in principle, then tried to discuss a controlled release schedule before the room had defined which warnings were mandatory. Ma interrupted. A worker needed to know when not to stand beside a task before a company decided how attractive its report would look. Chen accepted the correction and marked the point separately.

mine_p09_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_005.text: Lin asked whether declining a comparison role would affect her existing assistant shifts. Qiao said those shifts were accepted ordinary work and remained governed by their current terms. The proposed post was a different decision. Ren wrote the distinction in the public meeting note. Lin felt a knot loosen in her stomach. She had expected to need an elaborate defense of her livelihood. Qiao looked slightly offended that the fear had been plausible. Lin explained the earlier advertisement dispute, and Qiao acknowledged that a crossed out title could still leave an expectation in other people's minds.

mine_p09_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_006.text: Chen's second sheet described three ways Lin might approach the next inquiry meeting. One was from the worker side, through Luo's actual appointment and specific workers' consent. Another was a direct company factual comparison, with Chen remaining the company's advocate. The third was to consider only her own possible employment, taking no representative role. The sheet was a menu of meeting arrangements, not a source of automatic access. Each needed its own invitation and a defined task. Lin read the exclusions before the attractive headings. The limited roles could still change what she learned and whom she disappointed.

mine_p09_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_007.text: Sui wanted Lin in the company comparison because she had already handled careful receiving records. He said the worker side would suspect every supplier even when a damaged label came from ordinary storage. Ma said workers had reasons to be suspicious that did not require declaring suppliers villains. Lin remembered both the hammer and damp wedges. A chosen position would make some facts easier to see and other people less willing to speak. The room could not solve that by calling her neutral while assigning her a particular side's materials. She would have to name where she stood.

mine_p09_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_008.text: Mu arrived late carrying a repaired screen frame with Guan. She put it down outside the room before joining the public bench. Chen greeted her as a candidate, but she said she was here as a worker concerned with reading limited findings. The correction was mild and firm. Lin had sometimes thought of Mu mainly through the knee stool and delayed lessons. The repaired screen was an ordinary paid object she had completed while other people discussed future bodies. Mu asked who would decide which private statements could be copied. Nobody could answer everyone on a speaker's behalf.

mine_p09_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_009.text: The room became quiet enough to hear a cart passing the outer gate. Chen said every consenting source would need a named purpose, and private body material would remain under its separate method permission. He had previously used aggregate as if it solved all privacy. Mu asked whether a small group could be recognizable without names. Chen admitted it could. Lin admired the admission and wondered why it had taken a repair worker's question to produce it. Fluent advocacy was useful when challenged. Without challenge it could carry an attractive mistake smoothly past people who were tired.

mine_p09_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_010.text: Luo offered a short worker appointed listening session on Day 536. Three workers would describe specific practical concerns about future comparison tasks, each controlling what could be attributed. Lin could help organize their questions if she accepted that bounded voluntary role. It would not qualify her to diagnose injuries or authorize gallery entry. The session had no wage attached and would use an otherwise free half day. Luo would remain the appointed claim helper. Lin would lose that free study interval in exchange for hearing evidence she could not obtain from the company table.

mine_p09_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_011.text: Chen offered a company factual meeting on the same morning. He could show the permitted supply and schedule extracts relevant to the proposed comparison, with Sui and Fan answering within their own roles. The offer was not access to private worker statements, raw human examination material, or a bench for Lin's personal practice. It would also use the free half day without a new wage. She could ask harder supply questions than a public audience, but the company would know precisely which concerns she raised. Chen would record them as its retained advocate, not secretly become hers.

mine_p09_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_012.text: For her own employment questions Lin could instead receive the draft terms and a separate hour on Day 537. That choice took no side in the worker or company inquiry. It gave her a slower, narrower route to deciding whether she ever wanted the proposed post. She would not see the extra witness material or permitted supplier extracts offered in the other meetings. Declining those roles would protect free time and reduce authority; it would not preserve the same information by another name. Lin looked at the three times and saw an actual conflict rather than three versions of agreement.

mine_p09_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_013.text: Ma said a person who knew some receiving facts ought to help workers hear what the company was planning. Sui said the same experience belonged in the comparison where facts could correct worker assumptions. Lin could see how both appeals put duty around an invitation. Mu asked what Lin herself wanted to learn. The question made the room feel less crowded. Lin wanted to understand limits without lending her qualification to an unready advertisement. She also wanted to keep relationships that had begun in ordinary work. No choice would preserve every advantage, and pretending otherwise would hide its cost.

mine_p09_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_014.text: Chen asked whether they should talk privately before she decided. Lin refused the side conversation for now because the public scope questions were still unresolved. He accepted that without offense and stayed at the company table. Luo likewise did not ask her to promise representation beyond the three planned workers. Their restraint gave the decision room to become hers. She reviewed the ordinary shift roster to ensure no meeting overlapped paid work. Day 536 morning was free; her afternoon assistant turn and the week's second accepted half day remained as scheduled. Nothing had bought the same hours twice.

mine_p09_015.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_015.text: Fan Luwei had spoken little during the advocacy discussion. He finally said that an inquiry arrangement would not change the structural clearance of the gallery. People without the assigned permission would remain outside, whichever side's questions they carried. Lin was relieved to hear a boundary stated through his actual responsibility rather than a general moral claim. When an engineer closed a passage, a worker advocate could challenge the reasons through evidence, but could not open it by being persuasive. Chen wrote that into the public note beside the proposed later investigation role.

mine_p09_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_016.text: Chen mentioned an earlier contract argument he had settled badly. He had explained a replacement date so persuasively that two clients believed the other would bear the carrying charge. The written clause left that charge unresolved. He had to return to both rooms with a corrected explanation and lost part of his fee for the extra work. Lin appreciated the specific failure more than a claim that he always welcomed scrutiny. A man could be useful, interested, and fallible at once. The lesson was to keep asking where his fluent sentence ended and the actual term began.

mine_p09_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_017.text: Ma recalled the same dispute from the carrying workers' side. The late correction had arrived after an ordinary shift was planned, leaving people waiting without the expected work. Chen acknowledged that his fee adjustment had not automatically reimbursed their lost hours; those belonged to a separate actual settlement. The room stopped treating his admission as a complete moral repair. He accepted that too. Lin saw how a neat account of learning could hide another person's continuing loss. Whatever role she chose, she would need to follow the practical consequence rather than applaud the improved explanation alone.

mine_p09_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_018.text: Ren put the two histories beside each other in the public discussion note, with each speaker's permission. The carrier arrangement was not being reopened by this meeting, and no old wage was promised to Lin or anyone present. Its unresolved lessons concerned how the new proposal would name hours, charges, and ordinary interruptions before work began. Chen checked his own description for a phrase that still sounded too clean. He amended it without making Ma's account less uncomfortable. The public room became a little less spacious and a great deal easier to understand.

mine_p09_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_019.text: The meeting ended before anyone had to choose a method publication contract. Those terms were still future work. Ren read the factual note back, retaining the corrected title, the separate ordinary job, and the different invitations. The note recorded Chen's company retainer and Luo's limited worker appointment so a later reader would not treat either as universal authority. Lin heard her own name only beside her six pair qualification and possible meeting arrangement. That modest description felt safer than the earlier circuit assistant phrase. It left her able to accept a role without impersonating its outcome.

mine_p09_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_020.text: Outside the office Lei waited with a basket of repaired lamp fastenings. He had missed the meeting because actual repairs took the morning. Lin gave him the public summary and did not invent private details he had never heard. He asked which invitation she liked least. She said the worker side appealed to her, but she worried about becoming everyone's answer. Lei said the company side might do the same in a cleaner room. He could offer sympathy, not the correct decision. The lamp basket needed delivering before his paid interval ended, so they walked together toward the store.

mine_p09_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_021.text: A light rain began while they crossed the yard. Lin held the public note inside her coat and kept the private body book at the lodging. She could feel the difference between those two records without treating paper itself as a source of power. The first belonged to a meeting whose speakers had approved its factual summary. The second held her own preparation and sensory history. Any later proposed use would need a decision she had not yet made. Chen's offer did not collapse the distinction, and a worker's need for warnings did not erase it either.

mine_p09_022.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_022.text: At Han's table that evening Lin explained the three meeting choices to Mu. Mu said the worker role might make Lin useful where people distrusted polished language, but it could also turn ordinary help into expectations she could not meet. The company meeting would offer real supply evidence and leave workers unsure whose questions she carried. The personal hour would preserve time and distance, while losing specific information. Lin asked which Mu would choose. Mu said her own screen work already placed her on one side of some disputes. Lin's circumstances would have to answer for Lin.

mine_p09_023.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_023.text: Han overheard and offered the uncomplicated opinion that paid work should matter more than unpaid meetings. Lin pointed out that neither inquiry meeting paid a new wage, and the personal hour concerned only a draft job. Han revised his opinion to say the free time should then be cherished. It was a sensible household view, not a ruling on the public interest. Mu still thought some voluntary listening could be worth half a day. The disagreement did not need to end at the meal table. Lin slept with the invitations laid separately where morning would make their times clear.

mine_client_choice.speaker: narrator
mine_client_choice.text: Before leaving the lodging Lin checked the exact invitation she could accept. A worker role would mean assisting Luo's specified consenting questions; a company role would mean reviewing permitted factual extracts with its disclosed advocate; a personal role would mean considering only her own future terms. Ordinary wages, cultivation qualification, and basic safety warnings remained outside the bargain. What changed was the room she would enter, the evidence she could see, and the people entitled to expect her bounded help. She had enough information to choose, and no sentence that would make the costs disappear.

choices.text: Assist Luo's specifically consenting worker questions.
Review the company's permitted factual extracts with its disclosed advocate.
Take no inquiry role; consider only your own possible employment terms.

mine_client_worker.speaker: narrator
mine_client_worker.text: Lin chose the worker appointed listening session and told Luo before the morning began. She would help organize three consenting workers' questions, with no diagnostic claim and no permission to speak for absent people. Luo introduced each source separately rather than calling the group unanimous. Ma Lian wanted structural warning language clear enough to use at a shift boundary. Ou Sheng wanted an ordinary ventilation interruption considered before a comparison timetable was fixed. Deng Huan wanted restricted duty information kept distinct from a private tissue history. Lin heard three different concerns, not one worker voice.

mine_p09_worker_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_002.text: The listening room was a public side space off the surface yard, not an opened gallery. Luo placed a blank question sheet on the table and asked who wanted a name beside which statement. Ma consented to her practical timetable question being attributed. Ou allowed the ventilation question with his work role but not a copied private account of an earlier argument. Deng authorized only the current restricted duty concern. Lin used their exact scopes while drafting. She did not turn trust into a collection of intimate details just because the room felt more honest than the company office.

mine_p09_worker_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_003.text: Ma described how a warning arriving after the shift bell could fail even when its words were technically public. Workers assigned ordinary carrying might already be beside the comparison area. She wanted a posted stop condition before the activity, with the physical exit kept clear and an assigned ordinary response if it ended badly. Lin could write that question without promising to design the structural plan. Luo retained the worker appointment and would send the request to Qiao and Fan. The practical concern changed what the next meeting had to answer, instead of becoming a flattering story about Lin's sympathy.

mine_p09_worker_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_004.text: Ou worried that a candidate could mistake an ordinary altered air condition for a personal method failure or success. The ventilation keeper could report what his system actually did; he could not tell an examiner what happened inside a meridian. Lin wrote the separate evidence roles. Deng said that if ordinary restricted duties were posted, people should not be invited to infer the private injury from an attractive cultivation report. The three questions needed different recipients. Luo asked Lin to keep them separate, even though a single dramatic paragraph would have been easier to read aloud.

mine_p09_worker_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_005.text: During a break Chen came to the doorway with the company's proposed schedule. Luo asked him to leave the paper with the public questions rather than join the private source discussion. Chen complied. He looked surprised when Lin did not follow him out for an explanation. She had chosen a defined room, and its sources were still deciding their statement scopes. He was not excluded from answering public practical questions later. He was excluded from treating their unfinished consent conversation as material his client could hear. The distinction left Lin uncomfortable and the sources noticeably more willing to continue.

mine_p09_worker_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_006.text: Deng asked whether Lin believed the company would change anything. She said she could carry the questions accurately and insist the later answer address them. She could not guarantee a policy or employment outcome. Luo agreed and made the limit part of the session note. Deng seemed disappointed, then said he preferred that to a promise that would blame him if it failed. His restricted duty message remained the only body related material shared. The voluntary half day had given Lin evidence about ordinary work risks, not a private clinical archive or a mandate to cure them.

mine_p09_worker_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_007.text: At noon the sources read the drafted questions. Ma corrected a phrase that made a warning sound optional. Ou removed an anecdote he had not authorized. Deng kept his name off the public version. Lin made the corrections before Luo sent anything onward. The permitted question page went to the meeting contact under Luo's actual appointment; source notes stayed with their chosen custody. Lin retained only her authorized working copy. She had spent the free study interval and acquired responsibilities she could describe. That was the price of this access, and it was not paid through a cultivation bonus.

mine_p09_worker_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_008.text: Sui met her outside and said he had hoped she would look at the supplier extracts before hearing complaints. Lin said she had chosen the worker session and would not claim to know the unopened company material. He called that a poor way to remain neutral. She answered that she had not called herself neutral. She could still handle accurate receiving work on her paid shift. Sui accepted the copied manifest she brought him that afternoon, but spoke only about its numbers. The relationship cooled in an observable ordinary way without turning either person's facts false.

mine_p09_worker_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_009.text: Qiao acknowledged the permitted worker questions and arranged a later factual reply. She did not appoint Lin as a gallery investigator through the listening session. Fan would answer structural and access points within his responsibility, and any new investigation role would need its own scope. Luo thanked Lin for the bounded help and asked her to tell him if future employment talks changed whom she could represent. Lin agreed because the conflict was real, not because she expected a reward for candor. Her chosen side now had a small concrete public document and a reason to expect its followup.

mine_p09_worker_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_worker_010.text: At Han's room Lin tried to recover the free reading hour she had spent on the session. She was too tired after the actual assistant shift to learn unfamiliar references well. She reviewed only the empty stopping rehearsal and went to bed. The worker choice had cost time, opened consented practical evidence, and cooled one supplier relationship. It had also made Ma and Ou willing to ask her a question directly rather than through rumor. None of those consequences made her route more complete. They changed the life in which she would have to continue learning it.

mine_client_company.speaker: narrator
mine_client_company.text: Lin chose the company factual meeting with Chen's retainer named on the record. He greeted her in the covered inspection office on Day 536 and put only the permitted supply and schedule extracts on the table. Sui showed the damp wedge disposition and the difference between received quantity and structural acceptance. Fan explained the current clearance references without reopening the gallery. The access was real and narrow. Lin could now see which ordinary material delays the proposed comparison assumed away. She could not see worker private statements or borrow the supplier's bench for personal practice.

mine_p09_company_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_002.text: Chen began by explaining why the company wanted a comparison timetable that fit existing receiving work. Lin asked whether qualified recovery intervals were already priced into the proposed sequence. They were not yet shown. He called them an examiner matter, which was true but incomplete if the company scheduled the candidate. Fan agreed that an interrupted timetable could not be repaired by asking a body to perform sooner. Chen marked the dependency instead of defending the attractive early date. Lin had used the company access to make one planning gap visible inside the client's own record.

mine_p09_company_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_003.text: Sui showed a supply reference that Lin had not seen from the worker bench. The available compatible portions were finite, with matching condition checks and actual replacement lead times. Lin did not infer her internal usable quantity from the stock. She asked which account would pay for comparison portions if a future post were accepted. The proposal still needed that figure. Sui disliked the question because it made the stock seem less ready. Chen said readiness included assigning costs, and kept the unresolved account beside the material line. The company's clean room had acquired a useful untidy margin.

mine_p09_company_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_004.text: Fan refused to put a human method conclusion on the structural sheet. He could certify the ordinary fixture, exit, and isolation condition within his qualification. Wei and a clinician would remain responsible for their separate candidate evidence. Lin had heard this distinction in public and now saw how easily a private draft could blur it. She pointed to a combined approval box. Chen separated it into named roles before anyone signed. The change did not supply those approvals. It made their absence visible enough that the proposed schedule could not honestly call the whole comparison cleared.

mine_p09_company_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_005.text: At the interval Chen asked whether Lin wanted him to advise her on accepting the eventual post. She said he could explain his client's draft, but a company retainer could not quietly become independent advice to her in the same conversation. He agreed, with a rueful smile at how often fluent answers made that boundary feel unnecessary. They continued through factual questions. Lin learned more about the company's actual planning than a public note contained. The price was a record of her questions in a client held file and a clear limit on whose interests Chen represented.

mine_p09_company_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_006.text: Luo came to the doorway with the worker questions already permitted for public reply. Chen received them through the meeting contact. Lin did not open the private source notes or claim the worker appointment she had declined. Ma's timetable concern still deserved an answer, but Lin would hear it from this side's factual response rather than the consenting sources' preparation. She felt the loss when Deng's private question did not travel with his public concern. Choosing company evidence had not preserved worker access invisibly. Luo thanked her for naming the limit instead of borrowing his mandate through friendship.

mine_p09_company_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_007.text: By noon Lin had checked the extracts assigned for the meeting and marked unresolved costs, separate approvals, and the actual supply return. Her working copy contained only the permitted factual portions. Raw company material remained with its owner. Chen would answer the public safety questions through the named contact; Lin had not accepted a lab post or licensed her private method. Sui seemed pleased to have her ask precise questions inside the office rather than criticize its summary from outside. That warmer relationship could be useful later. It also meant workers would reasonably ask what company role she had taken.

mine_p09_company_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_008.text: Ma asked exactly that when Lin crossed the yard. Lin explained the disclosed company factual meeting and said her ordinary assistant shifts were still separate. Ma listened, then chose to send any later source concern through Luo rather than tell Lin informally. Lin could not demand trust on the strength of earlier receiving help. The practical loss was small enough to bear and large enough to notice. She had seen supply constraints and draft planning gaps. She would not now claim to carry every worker's private interpretation of them. Honest role information had changed who approached her.

mine_p09_company_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_009.text: Qiao reviewed the corrected draft before the afternoon shift. She accepted the separate approval boxes and the recovery dependency as useful questions, while leaving the future post undecided. Fan's access limits remained in force. Lin's company meeting did not authorize later gallery inquiry beyond its own new consent and clearance. Chen thanked her as a participant in a bounded factual review, without giving her a representative title. The public reply would now have fewer polished assumptions. Lin had spent the free half day improving a proposal she might still refuse, a cost that remained hers to consider.

mine_p09_company_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_company_010.text: At the lodging Lin laid the permitted factual copy beside her employment questions, away from the private body notes. Mu asked what she had learned. Lin could share the public planning corrections, not the protected supplier extracts merely because Mu was a friend. The boundary made their conversation shorter and more careful. Mu appreciated the corrected warning timetable but seemed cooler about the company meeting. Lin went to bed carrying useful access and a changed worker relationship. The choice had altered her evidence and obligations, while her incomplete route and existing six pair qualification remained exactly as before.

mine_client_own.speaker: narrator
mine_client_own.text: Lin chose the personal employment hour and declined both inquiry roles. She told Luo and Chen before Day 536 so neither reserved a source session around her. Luo thanked her for a clear answer and appointed another bounded helper from the workers who actually wished to attend. Chen left the factual review to Sui and Fan. Lin did not acquire either room's extra evidence by receiving their polite replies. She had protected the free morning and reduced what others could expect from her. The public safety questions would still need answers, with or without her at the table.

mine_p09_own_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_002.text: On the free morning she repaired the water damaged cover of her notebook with ordinary thread and helped Han move the drying line farther from the stove. Neither job qualified as an inquiry contribution. She could use the saved study interval for empty route orientation without sending qi through an unfamiliar bridge. The quiet felt valuable, then briefly selfish when she heard people passing toward the meeting. Lin wrote that feeling down and continued the assigned rehearsal. A voluntary role remained voluntary only if declining it did not require pretending she had made the same contribution anyway.

mine_p09_own_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_003.text: At her paid afternoon shift Sui asked whether she had heard the worker complaints. She had not attended the private listening session. He offered his own broad summary, and she treated it as his report rather than the sources' statements. When he asked what the company extracts had proved, she reminded him she had not reviewed those either. The unanswered questions made him impatient. Lin could still complete the receiving count in front of her. Accurate ordinary work was not a poor substitute for a representative role she had chosen not to hold; it was her actual accepted job.

mine_p09_own_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_004.text: Chen met her on Day 537 for the stated hour about her own possible employment. He named his company client again and gave her the draft terms he was permitted to explain. No laboratory post had yet been offered, and accepting the explanation transferred no technique rights. Lin asked what would happen if a later examination failed or recovery took months. The draft did not yet answer. Chen wrote the question for his client rather than assuring her the problem would never occur. She had obtained one concrete unresolved employment point without surrendering a private body record.

mine_p09_own_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_005.text: The next question concerned ordinary assistant shifts. Chen referred to Qiao's public clarification and confirmed the future comparison proposal was separate. Lin asked whether any paid post would require exclusive hours or confidential copies. The draft needed specific terms for both. He explained the possible company interest without calling it hers. Lin could now see which attractive phrases lacked an actual offer behind them. She did not have the supplier extracts that might explain the company's constraints or the worker notes that might explain distrust. Her personal hour gave her a narrower kind of knowledge.

mine_p09_own_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_006.text: Chen offered to arrange a later company review if she changed her mind. Lin said any new meeting would need fresh scope, timing, and consent; this declined invitation would not remain an invisible open door. He marked that plainly and returned to the unresolved employment questions. His fluency was useful when attached to a document he could amend. It was more dangerous when it sounded like certainty beyond the client's actual answer. Lin thanked him for recording the gaps. She did not hire him as independent counsel or grant him a worker mandate through the conversation.

mine_p09_own_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_007.text: Outside Luo told her the worker session had produced permitted practical questions and that he would carry them under his appointment. He shared the public version, not the private source preparation. Lin read the timetable and restricted duty concerns without guessing who had withheld a name. She could support clear safety warnings as an ordinary worker while remaining outside the representative role. The public page gave her less context than the private session would have supplied. She felt the loss when a question reminded her of Deng, and kept the inference out of her notes.

mine_p09_own_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_008.text: Ma greeted her politely on the next shift, then took an inquiry concern directly to Luo. Sui likewise brought supply draft questions to the company review rather than Lin's receiving table. Those were reasonable consequences of the decision she had named. They left Lin with fewer invitations and more uninterrupted work. She did not demand the closeness of participation while keeping the time of refusal. Lei asked whether she regretted the choice. She said she valued the free preparation morning and still wished she could hear everything. Wishing did not appoint her to the missing rooms.

mine_p09_own_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_009.text: Qiao thanked her for distinguishing the ordinary job from the possible post. The roster continued as accepted, with no punishment for declining a voluntary inquiry role. Qiao also said Lin should not answer later access questions as if she held an appointment she had refused. Any gallery investigation would require its own defined role and clearance. Lin accepted the limit. She had kept authority over her time and body notes, at the cost of particular evidence and representative expectations. The result was less dramatic than joining a side and just as capable of changing what happened next.

mine_p09_own_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_own_010.text: That evening she used the saved preparation notes for an ordinary empty rehearsal, then ate the room meal covered by her weekly board. Her private notebook stayed hers; the public questions and personal draft each remained within their own scope. Mu came to discuss the meeting but did not give her source material she lacked permission to receive. Lin listened to the public account and admitted what she had not seen. The personal choice had preserved a useful interval and a quieter role, without secretly granting the information, labor credit, or relationships of the two declined sessions.

mine_p09_after_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_001.text: The next public reply addressed the practical questions rather than the size of the listening audience. Qiao required warnings before activity, an assigned ordinary response, and a clear physical exit. Fan retained the structural isolation role. Ou's ventilation observation would describe actual conditions without diagnosing a human route. Chen recorded the company's answers with its retainer disclosed. Lin heard the reply from the evidence position she had actually chosen. A common safety baseline could be public while the private source rooms and supplier extracts remained distinct. Equal warnings did not make the earlier meeting choices identical.

mine_p09_after_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_002.text: On Day 539 Lin completed the week's other ordinary assistant half day and received its posted wage after the count closed. No voluntary meeting time appeared as paid labor in that entry. Ren checked the hours with her because the public discussion had lasted long enough for someone to assume all attendance was company work. She corrected the assumption before money moved. The two actual assistant half days still paid eight in total, and the four copper weekly board remained due. The curriculum, proposed post, and chosen inquiry arrangement had not created an unearned extra wage.

mine_p09_after_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_003.text: At the practice court Wei asked whether the meetings had changed Lin's ambition. Lin said they had made a possible future task seem nearer and more complicated. Wei asked whether any new input limit had been assessed. It had not. The existing half unit across four ordinary breaths, quarter unit useful task, complete stop, and grounded release still governed supervised preparation. Lin heard the question as practical care rather than a rebuke. Work could be attractive without making an incomplete method ready. The next lesson would use the actual condition she brought, not the company's need.

mine_p09_after_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_004.text: Mu arrived with an invoice for the repaired screen and joined the public waiting space after her ordinary work finished. Lin described only material she could properly share. Their friendship had room for questions that went unanswered. Mu said she preferred a boundary she could see to discovering later that every warm conversation had been copied into an advocate's file. Lin agreed, though she also knew a withheld detail could feel like distance. They ate after the appointment and argued about the meal portions instead. The smaller disagreement was a relief neither of them named.

mine_p09_after_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_005.text: Jia Wen posted a short notice for a Day 542 tailings discussion. Rain runoff had altered an ordinary surface observation near the moth habitat, and the disposal line might affect both cart work and the buffer. The notice promised no prophecy and claimed no human examination relevance. Lin recognized that her earlier habitat role would determine which actual notes or staff experience she could bring. She copied the time beside her shift schedule. Chen's proposal was one problem in the mine. Red earth, wet spoils, and the people moving through them continued to create another.

mine_p09_after_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_006.text: Sui read the notice and said cart detours were already costing enough time. Ma answered that a shortened route could still put workers beside unstable wet ground if it was laid carelessly. Jia had not yet presented the measured observations, and Fan had not cleared a new surface disposal line. Lin heard positions forming ahead of the evidence, as they had in the advocacy room. She did not try to become the one person who could decide every subject. Her chosen role had a scope. The new discussion would need its own qualified sources and actual ordinary costs.

mine_p09_after_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_007.text: At Han's room a pot lid clattered from the shelf and everyone looked up before realizing what had fallen. The ordinary interruption made Lin laugh at how alert the household had become since the scorched shirt. Han fixed the loose shelf fastening before replacing the lid. Lei checked the lamp without being asked. Lin put down her notebook until the work was finished, then resumed the empty rehearsal from its beginning. Familiar life was not noise she would eventually outgrow. It was the condition in which a reliable method had to remain honest about starting and stopping.

mine_p09_after_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p09_after_008.text: Before bed she wrote the consequence of the meeting choice in one concrete paragraph: the room entered, the permitted evidence received, the free time spent or kept, and the people entitled to expect bounded help. She wrote no claim to see material from a declined invitation. The record would matter when the inquiry returned. Lin turned the page to the tailings notice and set the old questions behind it. The mine was not a single examination waiting for her success. It was many people's work, with a living seam of needs she could join only in particular ways.
